sections.title: 1. The diagnosis
paragraphs: For too long the Latin American tech map was drawn around Bogotá, Medellín, São Paulo, Buenos Aires and Mexico City. The Colombian Caribbean, with its talent, its universities, its open culture and its port-city position, was left as rhythm, sea and plantain fields, not as code, capital or frontier innovation. That reading does not hold for lack of people, but for a historical absence of ecosystem infrastructure: sustained communities, current education, patient capital and a public narrative.

The result was a paradox: talent that trains and leaves; companies that could be born here and scale with their own identity; and an internal story that treated innovation as something that “happens in other capitals”. Recent facts —Barranqui-IA, Costa Digital, Caribe Ventures, alliances with Google and the Atlántico Governor’s Office, the accumulated institutional press— contradict that reading. The map is being redrawn.

sections.title: 2. The fundamentals
paragraphs: The moment is technical and cultural at once. Agentic AI changed the balance between talent and product: fewer people build more, and less capital goes further. You no longer need the density of a megacity to produce global companies, but you do need a community that connects learning, opportunity and trust.

The Colombian Caribbean has universities, competitive costs, a strong cultural identity, a tech diaspora ready to come back, and a political moment aligned with the TIC Secretariat, City Hall and multilateral partners. It is also a port city: a way out to Central America, the insular Caribbean and the United States.

sections.title: 3. The thesis: Epicentro Tech
paragraphs: Epicentro Tech is not Silicon Valley, and it is not a copy of Medellín. It is the explicit bet that Barranquilla and the Caribbean region be recognized as a first-order Latin American tech node: with its character, its companies, its events, its talent and its own way of relating to the world.

In practice, Epicentro Tech means designing education, innovation, capital and community at the same time, so a founder’s cycle is possible without unnecessary friction: learn, build, connect, fund and scale while staying anchored to the territory.

sections.title: 4. Costa Digital and its four capacities
paragraphs: Costa Digital is the innovation and technology transformation center of the Colombian Caribbean. It lives in Casa Tech, one of the 39 heritage houses of El Prado, in Barranquilla, and is operated by Fundación Código Abierto. Under one roof it articulates:
items: Education · Tech Centre. Trains professionals to market standards with experiential methods; AI Engineer as the anchor track, and AI as a daily tool.
Innovation · Ciudad Inmersiva. Applied AI lab; its AI Sprint program delivers a trained agent in three weeks.
Capital · Caribe Ventures. A Delaware-structured pre-seed fund with proprietary dealflow across +3,000 active people.
Community. The center’s circulatory system: GDG Barranquilla, Tech Nights, Cursor Meetup, TechCaribe Fest and Barranqui-IA.

sections.title: 5. The next wave: why Barranquilla, why now
paragraphs: Behind software there is a deeper wave: robotics and physical AI. The generation of models we train today will give birth to the generation of machines that come next. The question is from which territory they will be assembled and programmed. The Colombian Caribbean has an asset few Latin American cities can match: industrial DNA. Barranquilla was Colombia’s industrial capital and still holds logistics infrastructure, technical knowledge and a producer’s vocation.

The long thesis is deliberate: today we invest in the software and AI generation that will give birth to Latin American robotics. Why the Caribbean: because it has a port, technical talent, competitive costs and a strong cultural brand. Why now: because the agentic-AI window opens possibilities that did not exist a decade ago, and because there is political and institutional alignment to scale.

sections.title: 6. The call
paragraphs: This manifesto convenes distinct and complementary profiles. If you are a founder: there is a thesis and aligned capital to build from here with AI. If you are an LP or investor: there is dealflow, international structure and an explicit regional thesis. If you are diaspora: there are roles, a physical house, community and reasons to come back. If you are young talent: there is training, mentorship and living communities. If you are a company or government: there is a serious territorial counterpart for adoption and regional dynamization programs.
The Caribbean does not need more scattered goodwill. It needs articulation. Costa Digital is that articulation. And Casa Tech is where the next chapter of the Latin American map begins, physically.

q1.question: Is Costa Digital a company?
q1.answer: Costa Digital is the technology cluster of the Colombian Caribbean, a brand that represents the ecosystem. Membership is operated by Ciudad Inmersiva SAS, in partnership with Fundación Código Abierto and ecosystem organizations. Part of the revenue goes to impact programs executed by FCA.

q2.question: Does membership guarantee discounts/benefits?
q2.answer: Benefits and discounts are offered by ecosystem allies and are subject to availability. Costa Digital facilitates access to these benefits, but does not guarantee specific results. We connect the right people at the right time.

q3.question: Can I cancel at any time?
q3.answer: Yes, you can cancel your membership at any time. Cancellation is monthly and does not require a long-term commitment.

q4.question: What's the difference between Community and Builder?
q4.answer: Builder includes everything from Community, plus preferential access to paid events, closed dynamics, basic visibility as an active member, early access to programs (Tech Centre, Ciudad Inmersiva), preferential pricing on Parla Startupera, and eligibility for premium programs like Synergy.

q5.question: How does it work for companies?
q5.answer: The Company plan is designed for companies and organizations seeking visibility, access to talent, private B2B events and activations with communities. It includes featured profile, access to dealflow and Caribe Ventures when applicable. For more complex open innovation programs, there is the Enterprise/Innovation option that includes corporate challenges, labs and demo days.

grace.name: Grace Torres
grace.role: Cofounder · CEO · General director of the Innovation Center
grace.bio: A lawyer specialized in administrative law, and a singer with her solo project Grace. She has spent three years as operations director and is now CEO of Fundación Código Abierto. She is also an entrepreneur.

anuar.name: Anuar Harb
anuar.bio: He has spent ten years in technology. Born in Mexico, he arrived here by the turns of life. Once he understood the difference between a chuzo and a salchipapa, he felt barranquillero. With his vision and his craziness he is building ecosystem through Tech Centre, Ciudad Inmersiva, Caribe Ventures and Fundación Código Abierto.

why.title: Why we do this
why.operatedBy: This innovation center is operated by Fundación Código Abierto.
why.lead: Technology is the industry of opportunity. We do it from the Caribbean so the people who train here can stay to build and leave something behind.

talent.title: So talent does not have to leave
talent.text: For years the story was train and migrate. We want the people who learn in the house to work, found and scale without leaving the region.

house.title: Because a house was missing
house.text: Community, education, capital and a public story. Without that, the map gets drawn in other cities. Costa Digital is that articulation, under one roof in El Prado.

lives.title: Because it changes real lives
lives.text: Every scholarship, Tech Night and program moves someone concrete. More than 100 people trained with us now work in technology.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: What people usually ask when they arrive at the house.

items.a: The innovation and technology transformation center of the Colombian Caribbean. It lives in Casa Tech, in El Prado (Barranquilla), and is operated by Fundación Código Abierto. Under one roof it articulates education (Tech Centre), innovation (Ciudad Inmersiva), capital (Caribe Ventures) and community.

The bet that Barranquilla and the Caribbean become a first-order Latin American tech node, with its own character and way of relating to the world. It is not a replica of Medellín or Silicon Valley. It means being able to learn, build, connect, fund and scale without leaving the territory.

Fundación Código Abierto, a nonprofit. Grace Torres is cofounder, CEO and general director of the Innovation Center. Anuar Harb is cofounder and CTO. Ciudad Inmersiva is the software and applied-AI lab.

items.q: Where is it? Can I come without a membership?
items.a: Cra. 50 #72-126, El Prado, Barranquilla. It is one of the neighborhood’s 39 heritage houses. 404 Café is open without a membership: you can read, cowork or have a drink. Thursdays fill up. Write us on WhatsApp (+57 318 752 9000) or come by.

A cafeteria that sustains the house. A place to connect, read about tech and feel at home. It is run by Cristian Lugo, a professional barista and bartender, founder of Instituto del Cóctel in Barranquilla.

items.q: What events happen at the house?
items.a: Tech Nights on the third Saturday of each month, Barranqui-IA, TechCaribe Fest, GDG Barranquilla, Cursor Meetup and Thursday Cowork. Community is the center’s circulatory system.

You can create an account, ask for a membership (the first 60 are Believers), study at Tech Centre, come to the café or write on WhatsApp. If you are a founder or investor, there is a thesis and capital at Caribe Ventures. If you are a company or government, there is a territorial counterpart for programs.

Grace Torres and Anuar Harb, cofounders. Grace is a lawyer specialized in administrative law, an entrepreneur and CEO of Fundación Código Abierto. Anuar has spent ten years in technology, was born in Mexico and feels barranquillero: he builds ecosystem through Tech Centre, Ciudad Inmersiva, Caribe Ventures and Fundación Código Abierto.
